title: Byte Ledger Attribution Carousel: interactive token-cost exploration and export
creator: Sophie Chen
description: Design and prototype a compact, embeddable 'Byte Ledger Attribution Carousel' widget for Redwood Console that lets engineers and finance teams explore token-level cost breakdowns, trace cost lineage across messages and prompts, and export role-aware CSV/Parquet slices. The carousel will be used in dashboards, rollout pages, and the cost export workflow.
background: Customers ask for fast, focused ways to understand which prompts, model variants, and routing policies drive unit cost. Existing console views are table-heavy and require heavy filtering. The goal is a visually compact exploration surface that surfaces marginal cost contributors, supports quick comparisons between model variants and rollout buckets, and produces exportable, permission-aware line-item exports for chargeback.
goals: Provide an at-a-glance ranked list of top token cost contributors (by prompt slice, model, route)
Surface marginal cost delta when toggling pricing slabs, caching and batching settings
Support role-aware exports that obfuscate or redacts sensitive request text for non-billing roles
Be embeddable on Dashboard, Rollout Overview, and Chargeback Export flows
success_criteria: Prototype validated in user research with N=6 platform engineers/product finance; at least 4/6 can identify top-3 cost drivers in <90s
Design passes accessibility audit (contrast and keyboard nav)
Export CSV/Parquet matches accounting schema and includes variant-level pricing columns
acceptance_criteria: Carousel shows up to 6 cards with ranked token-cost contributors and key KPIs (tokens, unit price, total cost, marginal delta)
Toolbar includes: time window, aggregation dimension selector (prompt, model, route, user), comparison toggle, export button
Export supports two presets: Detailed (full request hash + token counts) and Redacted (no request text, aggregated keys only)
Design specifies role-based hiding rules: viewer, analyst, billing; visuals indicate redacted fields
Figma prototype with interactive toggles and export dialog linked; developer handoff tokens annotated
tasks: Finalize card data schema with infra (fields: slice_key, prompt_hash, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, unit_price, cost_total, marginal_delta, export_flags)
Prototype two export presets in design and validate schema with finance
Create accessibility checklist and run contrast/keyboard tests on prototype
Handoff tokens and interaction spec to frontend (React) and runtime teams for API contract

decisions: Use two-tier export presets (Detailed, Redacted) rather than arbitrary column chooser to keep legal/finance safe
Show marginal delta as absolute cost delta and as a percent tooltip to reduce cognitive load
Embed carousel as a single reusable component with a compact card API for reuse on Rollouts and Dashboard
risks: Performance: querying token-level slices for long time windows could be slow — need telemetry and a paginated /aggregate endpoint
Privacy: raw request text in Detailed export may require additional retention checks — security review required
Interpretability: marginal delta needs clear copy/context to avoid misattributing cost to non-modal factors
